identity.name: Free France
alt_names: Provisional Government of the French Republic

land.text: Chad, Cameroon, the Middle Congo and Ubangi-Shari, the first colonies to rally in August 1940

predecessors.note: Free France began in London in June 1940 without land; its first territory came from the French Africa row of Cliopatria (Cameroon, Chad, Congo and Ubangi-Shari in August 1940, Gabon on 12 November 1940).

land.text: France, liberated in 1944, and the empire under the Provisional Government of the French Republic created on 3 June 1944

successors.note: The Free France page: the Provisional Government 'was officially created by the CNFL and succeeded it on 3 June 1944'. Cliopatria has no row for it and starts the Fourth Republic in 1945.

land.text: the equatorial lands and Djibouti, which Cliopatria returns to its French Africa row in 1943

successors.note: Cliopatria's French Africa row is 11,072,843 km2 in 1943 against 8,717,417 km2 in 1942.

capitals.name: Brazzaville
capitals.note: Infobox: 'Brazzaville (de jure and de facto) (1940–1942)'; 'Paris (de jure) London (de facto) (until November 1942)', where the exile government sat.

rulers.name: Charles de Gaulle
rulers.title: Leader of Free France
rulers.note: 'On 18 June 1940, General de Gaulle spoke to the French people via BBC radio'; the page extract opened does not list the co-presidency of the French Committee of National Liberation from 1943.

correction.text: the Cliopatria 1940 shape without Gabon and with Chad: Chad, Cameroon, the Congo and Ubangi-Shari as they stood at the end of August 1940; Gabon is added on 12 November

keyframe_review.note: Cliopatria's 1,654,263 km2 shape for 1940 holds Cameroon, the Congo, Ubangi-Shari and Gabon but not Chad, the first colony to rally (26 August 1940), and it holds Gabon, which stayed with Vichy until 12 November 1940 ('By the end of August, all of French Equatorial Africa' except Gabon). So Chad is added and Gabon taken out until the ledger's November event. The page gives no area to compare.

correction.text: the Cliopatria 1941 shape plus the whole of Chad

keyframe_review.note: The 1941 shape (2,355,528 km2) adds Chad but only its southern 57 percent (gazetteer overlay: 2,615 of 4,576 cells); the page says the colony as a whole pledged allegiance on 26 August 1940, so northern Chad is added. Syria and Lebanon, taken in June-July 1941, are a vassal tint in the ledger, not part of this shape.

correction.text: the Cliopatria 1942 shape plus the whole of Chad; narrowed to the year 1942

keyframe_review.note: Valid for 1942 only. The 2,377,926 km2 shape adds French Somaliland (Djibouti, 89 of 95 cells), ousted from Vichy on 28 December 1942, and the Saint-Pierre and Miquelon bbox. In 1943 Cliopatria's French Africa row takes the equatorial lands and Djibouti back (the French Africa dossier of af-08 has the gain), so 1943 needs the new keyframe free-french_1943. Whole Chad is added as in 1941.

correction.text: French Guiana, Guadeloupe, Martinique and Saint-Pierre and Miquelon, the Free French land of 1943

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: after the French Committee of National Liberation of 3 June 1943 the equatorial lands rejoin French Africa in Cliopatria; what is left is the Americas, which 'finally joined Free France in the first months of 1943', and Saint-Pierre and Miquelon (24 December 1941). This is the Cliopatria 1944 shape.

89,085 km2: French Guiana (97 percent of its 298 cells), Guadeloupe and Martinique, plus Saint-Pierre and Miquelon. The Provisional Government was created on 3 June 1944; the page gives no area to compare, and mainland France, liberated from June, is in no Cliopatria row for 1944.

region.text: the French South Pacific colonies and French India

ledger.note: Summer 1940: French India and the South Pacific colonies join. 'French India and the French South Pacific colonies … joined Free France in the summer 1940'; the New Hebrides condominium joined on 20 July. The page gives no month for the French colonies, so none is recorded. Cliopatria has no shape for these islands and Pondicherry; the region is the researcher's reading of 'French South Pacific colonies' as New Caledonia and French Polynesia.

region.text: Chad, Cameroon, the Middle Congo and Ubangi-Shari, its first territory

ledger.note: 18 June 1940: de Gaulle's appeal at the BBC founds Free France. 'Free France was established as a government-in-exile in London in June 1940 after the Fall of France'; it held no land until August. The region is the core of its first rallies.

region.text: the colony of Chad under Félix Éboué

ledger.note: 26 August 1940: Chad rallies. 'On 26 August, with the help of his top military official, Éboué pledged his colony's allegiance to Free France.'

region.text: French Cameroon, a League of Nations mandate

ledger.note: 27 August 1940: Cameroon rallies. 'In 1940, French Cameroon rallied to Free France'; Leclerc's troops 'landed at Douala, capturing it on 27 August', then Yaoundé, where the pro-Vichy governor surrendered the civil administration.

region.text: the French Congo (Middle Congo), with Brazzaville

ledger.note: 29 August 1940: the Middle Congo rallies. The Vichy France page lists 'French Chad on 26 August 1940, French Congo on 29 August 1940, and Ubangi-Shari on 30 August 1940'.
30 August 1940: Ubangi-Shari rallies. 'By the end of August, all of French Equatorial Africa' except Gabon was with Free France (Free France page).

region.text: Gabon, loyal to Vichy until November 1940

ledger.note: 27 October 1940: the Free French attack Vichy Gabon. Gabon 'had to be occupied by military force between 27 October and 12 November 1940'; on 8 November 1940 Free French forces under de Gaulle and Kœnig were in action there.
12 November 1940: Gabon falls to Free France, completing the equatorial colonies. The Free France page: 'There was better news in November 1940 when the FFF achieved victory at the Battle of Gabon'.
12 November 1940: the Battle of Gabon ends.

region.text: Syria and Lebanon, the French mandate

ledger.note: 8 June 1941: the Syria-Lebanon campaign begins. 'Hostilities commenced on 8 June 1941' between British Empire forces including Free French units and Vichy France; 'Battle of Damascus' 18-21 June.

region.text: Syria and Lebanon, the French mandate

ledger.note: 14 July 1941: the Vichy forces give in. 'At one minute past midnight on 12 July, a ceasefire came into effect'; the Convention of Acre was signed on 14 July; 'Syria and Lebanon taken over by Free France'.

region.text: Syria and Lebanon, the French mandate

ledger.note: July 1941: Syria and Lebanon pass under Free France. Infobox: 'Syria and Lebanon taken over by Free France'; the Free France page: 'Free France would control both Syria and Lebanon until they became independent in 1946 and 1943 respectively'; on 26 November Catroux 'recognized the independence of Syria and Lebanon in the name of the Free French movement'. Drawn as a lighter tint: the mandate keeps its own Cliopatria row (to 1945) and its dossier calls the change a rename.
24 December 1941: Saint-Pierre and Miquelon. The islands 'joined the Free French after an "invasion" on 24 December 1941'.
13 July 1942: Free France becomes Fighting France. 'On 13 July 1942, "Free France" was officially renamed Fighting France (France combattante)'. Same state, same colour.

28 December 1942: French Somaliland leaves Vichy. The infobox gives 'British occupation: December 28, 1942'; the Free France page: 'On 28 December, after a prolonged blockade, the Vichy forces in French Somaliland were ousted'. Cliopatria's 1942 shape includes Djibouti; the French Africa dossier records the British occupation of the same day.

First months of 1943: the French Americas join. Guadeloupe, Martinique and French Guiana 'finally joined Free France in the first months of 1943'. The page extract gives no day; Martinique is named for July 1943 in another passage.

region.text: Cameroon, Gabon, the Congo, Ubangi-Shari, Chad and Djibouti

ledger.note: 1943: the equatorial lands and Djibouti go back to French Africa. Cliopatria's French Africa row grows by about 2.35 M km2 in 1943 (the Free French shape of 1942-1943); the Free France page dates only the French Committee of National Liberation to 3 June 1943 and does not list the colonies, so the link and the year are the researcher's bridge. Page silent.
3 June 1943: the French Committee of National Liberation. The page's infobox: 'National Liberation Committee: 3 June 1943' ('officially founded on 3 June 1943').

region.text: Syria and Lebanon, the French mandate

ledger.note: June 1944: the Free French hold on Syria and Lebanon passes to the Provisional Government. Lebanon became independent on 22 November 1943 (Syria-Lebanon campaign page) and Syria in 1946 (Free France page); the mandate row runs to 1945.

region.text: the Free French lands of 1944: French Guiana, Guadeloupe, Martinique and Saint-Pierre and Miquelon

ledger.note: 3 June 1944: the Provisional Government of the French Republic takes over. It 'was officially created by the CNFL and succeeded it on 3 June 1944'. The same regime continues under another name; Cliopatria ends its Free French row in 1944 and draws the Fourth Republic from 1945. Syria and Lebanon, held as a tint, pass with it.

wars.name: Battle of Gabon
wars.outcome: Free French victory: Gabon, the last of the equatorial colonies, is occupied between 27 October and 12 November 1940.
wars.note: The Free France page dates the victory to November 1940.

wars.name: Battle of Dakar
wars.outcome: Failure: 'On 23 September 1940, the Royal Navy and Free French forces under Gaulle launched Operation Menace'; 'British and Free French forces withdrew on 25 September'. No land changed hands.

wars.name: Syria-Lebanon campaign

zones.text: Syria and Lebanon, the French mandate

wars.outcome: Allied victory: ceasefire 12 July and the Convention of Acre on 14 July 1941; 'Syria and Lebanon taken over by Free France'.
wars.note: 8 June to 14 July 1941; British, Australian, Indian and Free French forces against Vichy forces.

wars.name: Battle of Madagascar
wars.outcome: British and Commonwealth conquest of Vichy Madagascar in Operation Ironclad ('From 5 May to 6 November 1942'). The pages opened do not date its handover to the Free French, and Cliopatria draws Madagascar in its French Africa row throughout, so no zone is recorded.

certainty.note: The equatorial colonies' frontiers were administrative lines, approximate on the map; the Syrian and Lebanese frontiers are those of the mandate. The French Americas are islands and a coastal colony with settled borders.

sources.title: Free France
sources.note: Founding, capitals, renaming 13 July 1942, CFLN 3 June 1943, Provisional Government 3 June 1944, Chad 26 August, Gabon November 1940, Saint-Pierre and Miquelon 24 December 1941, the Americas 1943. No area figure.

sources.title: Vichy France
sources.note: Free French rallies: Chad 26, Congo 29, Ubangi-Shari 30 August 1940; Gabon 27 October to 12 November 1940; Dakar; Madagascar.

sources.title: French Cameroons
sources.note: Cameroon rallied in 1940; Douala taken 27 August.

sources.title: Syria-Lebanon campaign
sources.note: 8 June to 14 July 1941; Syria and Lebanon taken over by Free France; independence recognised 26 November 1941.

notes:
Page budget (up to 5) spent on Free France, Vichy France (shared with vichy-france), French Cameroons, Syria-Lebanon campaign and French Somaliland.

Cliopatria problems: (1) the 1940 shape has Gabon (Vichy until 12 November 1940) and lacks Chad (26 August); (2) the 1941 shape has only the southern 57 percent of Chad; (3) the 1942-1943 shape covers 1943 too, but in 1943 Cliopatria's French Africa row takes back the same equatorial lands, so the two rows overlap; this dossier narrows 1942 to one year and adds a 1943 keyframe for the Americas; (4) Syria and Lebanon (1941), the French Pacific colonies and French India are in no Free French shape; (5) mainland France in 1944 has no row (Vichy ends 1943, Fourth Republic begins 1945) and the Provisional Government of June 1944 is no Cliopatria row: a gap for eu-22.
Counterparts: gains from french-africa mirror that dossier's losses (1940-08 Cameroon, Chad, Congo, Ubangi-Shari; 1940-11 Gabon). The Americas, Saint-Pierre and Miquelon and the Pacific/India colonies name vichy-france, whose dossier carries the matching losses of the Americas.

Not settled: Madagascar (British conquest 5 May to 6 November 1942, Free French rule from a date no page opened gives), Réunion, French West Africa (loyal to Vichy until November 1942 per the Free France page; joined the Allies afterwards), North Africa from Operation Torch (8 November 1942), the Fezzan (January 1943, in the French Africa dossier), Corsica (the Free France page: 'In September 1943, the liberation of Corsica from Italian occupation began') and the New Hebrides condominium (20 July 1940, a Franco-British condominium: no event). A gap-filler should open Battle of Madagascar and Liberation of Corsica.
Event order: the summer-1940 event has no month and so sorts ahead of the June founding; the Pacific colonies joined after the founding.
Gazetteer names: 'Pondicherry' is used as a place (7 cells at 30 km); the other names resolve.
